A1.justification: Both complete 20-page PDFs describe the same axiomatic-training research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original experiments training transformers on synthetic causal axioms and fine-tuning Llama, with results on synthetic generalization tests, CLEAR, and Corr2Cause.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and reports revised Corr2Cause results, alongside synthetic and CLEAR evaluations.

M1.justification: Synthetic triplet generation, the 67M GPT-2-style architecture, custom tokenizer, label-prediction loss, positional-encoding variants, and LoRA fine-tuning procedure remain unchanged. Architecture details move from Section 5.2 to Section 4.2; no new method component is established.

E1.justification: Both evaluate synthetic transitivity and d-separation with retained structural and naming shifts, CLEAR d-separation Yes/No and multiple-choice questions, and Corr2Cause. New benchmark examples and proposed verifier applications do not establish additional evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain GPT-4, Gemini Pro, and Phi-3 for transitivity, and GPT-4 and base Llama for d-separation and benchmark evaluations. V3 explains why only GPT-4 was selected among the larger-model baselines for d-separation; that comparator selection already appears in v2.

E3.justification: Corr2Cause transitivity fine-tuning changes from a reported 300k examples in v2 Table 5 to 175k in v3 Table 4. V3 also standardizes the model specification to Llama-3-8B, whereas v2 alternates between Llama-3.1 and Llama-3. These revisions do not establish whether experiments were rerun or the underlying model changed.

E4.justification: V2 Appendix H's relationship-template F1 and accuracy analyses, Figures A2–A3, are removed. These examined which Corr2Cause relationship types benefited from each fine-tuning dataset. The structural-generalization, data-diversity, and positional-encoding analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run estimates, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. Both use terms such as significant without adding statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Corr2Cause results are substantially revised: base/d-separation/transitivity F1 values are 0.18/0.20/0.37 in v2 and 0.11/0.23/0.32 in v3. Transitivity precision/recall/accuracy change from 0.28/0.57/0.70 to 0.20/0.93/0.39, alongside the revised training count; these are replacement results, not controlled performance changes. GPT-4's F1 remains 0.29. Template-level results disappear. CLEAR scores remain unchanged, while its stated multiple-choice improvement is corrected from 20% to 17%.

T1.justification: The stability assumption, causal-irrelevance and transitivity formulations, d-separation definition, Markov definitions, and perturbation formalization are retained. Appendix terminology and notation corrections do not introduce substantive mathematical changes, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The central generalization and benchmark-transfer claims remain. V3 restates the headline Corr2Cause benefit as about 20 F1 points over base Llama and removes the conclusion's broad attribution of correlation inference to the 67M model. Its expanded Figure 1 introduces an accuracy-improvement claim that conflicts with the revised Corr2Cause table.

C2.justification: V3 more explicitly qualifies the from-scratch model's performance as branching complexity increases and contrasts it with fine-tuned Llama. It explains choosing F1 because of label imbalance, removes template-specific interpretations and the conjecture about GPT-4 learning axioms from web data, and adds prospective verifier and pre-RL applications.

D1.justification: V3 adds four A6000 GPUs for fine-tuning, explicitly states synthetic-data release, and changes the printed repository path from CausalAxioms to Causal_Axioms. It drops v2's from-scratch 100-epoch/AdamW specification. The retained three-GPU statement conflicts with the new four-GPU disclosure.

R1.justification: V3 adds Gandhi et al. (2025) to motivate axiomatic training before reinforcement learning and more explicitly contrasts its synthetic training with direct Corr2Cause fine-tuning. Most other reference changes consolidate duplicates or update publication metadata for retained works.

P1.justification: V3 substantially rewrites the benchmark exposition and discussion, expands the introduction and fine-tuning explanation, and replaces the generic impact statement. Architecture and baseline material move into Section 4, zero-shot prompting moves to Appendix B, and Section 7 gains explicit dataset/setup and results subdivisions.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn and moved into the introduction, adding the Llama fine-tuning and benchmark pathway. The two Corr2Cause performance plots are removed, and a benchmark-example figure is added. Main Tables 3–5 are reordered and recaptioned, substantially revising the visual presentation while most numerical table structures and Figures 2–3 remain.

improvement.justification: V3 clarifies benchmark evaluation and the small model's limitations, but removes Corr2Cause breakdowns and v2's from-scratch optimizer/epoch details. Its replacement Corr2Cause results show F1 gains alongside accuracy losses that are not discussed, while the new Figure 1 claims accuracy improvements. The unexplained result and training-specification revisions, together with these opposing clarity and evidential-support changes, prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
